title: How few steps to 3 to the 16th?
hook: Sixteen threes multiplied together. You may reuse anything you have already made.

knows: that a power is repeated multiplication
doesNotKnow: that a result can be reused (squared) to double the exponent

objective: The learner can reach 3^16 in 4 multiplications by squaring (3^2, 3^4, 3^8, 3^16) and explain why 3 cannot be enough: each multiplication at most doubles the exponent.

claims.source: 3^a × 3^a = 3^(2a); 1 → 2 → 4 → 8 → 16. Demo.tsx SQ_STEPS = log2(16) = 4. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-13 (pass 6): Re-derived; no issue.

claims.text: Multiplying by 3 one step at a time takes 15 multiplications to reach 3^16.
claims.source: Each step raises the exponent by 1, from 1 to 16: 15 steps. Demo.tsx ONE_STEPS = GOAL − 1. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-13 (pass 6): Re-derived; no issue.

claims.text: No multiplication can more than double the largest exponent you have, so 3 steps reach at most 3^8, and 4 is the fewest for 3^16.
claims.source: Multiplying 3^a × 3^b gives 3^(a+b) ≤ 3^(2 max). After k steps the largest exponent is ≤ 2^k; 2^3 = 8 < 16. Builder's exhaustive addition-chain search in Node: shortest chain for 16 has length 4. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-13 (pass 6): The shortest addition chain to 16 has length 4 (exponent at most doubles each step).

claims.text: Reaching 3^n this way takes about as many squarings as times you can halve n (log₂ n), plus a few extra multiplies when n is not a power of 2; for a power in the millions that is a few dozen steps.
claims.source: Square-and-multiply (binary method) uses ⌊log₂ n⌋ squarings plus (number of 1 bits − 1) multiplications (Knuth, TAOCP Vol. 2, 4.6.3). For n = 1,000,000: 19 squarings + 6 multiplies = 25. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-13 (pass 6): Node: for n = 10^6, 19 squarings + 6 multiplies = 25. Across exponents up to about 16 million the count runs 22 to 46, which fits 'a few dozen'.

recall.question: Using squaring, about how many multiplications does 5^1024 need?
recall.why: 1024 = 2^10, so squaring ten times doubles the exponent from 1 to 1024.
